description.short_caption: Skin lesions on the forearm, including a sutured wound and an erythematous pustule.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a forearm with two distinct lesions. One lesion is a sutured wound with surrounding erythema, suggesting recent trauma or surgical intervention. The second lesion is a raised, erythematous pustule with a central area of necrosis or crusting, indicative of a possible infectious process. The surrounding skin appears mildly erythematous but otherwise intact.
visible_findings: raised pustule with central necrosis or crusting

Case_12008/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy, DPAS stain, with arrow showing organisms.

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy with DPAS stain showing fungal organisms (arrow).
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification histopathology image of a skin biopsy stained with DPAS (diastase-periodic acid-Schiff). The tissue demonstrates an inflammatory infiltrate with numerous darkly stained fungal organisms visible, highlighted by the DPAS stain. The arrow points to a cluster of these organisms, which appear as round to oval structures with a magenta hue. The background shows connective tissue and inflammatory cells.
visible_findings: arrow pointing to a cluster of organisms

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy with H&E stain showing inflammatory infiltrate and multinucleated giant cells.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue demonstrates a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous lymphocytes, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells. There is also evidence of dermal fibrosis and some areas of necrosis. The multinucleated giant cells suggest a granulomatous inflammatory process, which may be seen in infectious or non-infectious conditions.

description.short_caption: GMS stain of lung tissue showing fungal organisms.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathological image of lung tissue stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stain. The tissue shows numerous round to oval fungal organisms, which are stained black against a green background. The red arrow highlights a cluster of these organisms. The GMS stain is commonly used to identify fungal elements in tissue sections.
visible_findings: round to oval fungal organisms stained black
green background typical of GMS stain
red arrow pointing to fungal cluster
